    A distributive ideal lattice of a finite-dimensional algebra is finite #

    For an ideal K ≠ B choose an ideal J > K of least dimension. For ideals I ≥ K the meet I ⊓ J is K or J, and I ↦ (I ⊓ J, I ⊔ J) is injective by distributivity, so the ideals above K are finite when those above J are (finite_twoSidedIdeal_of_isDistribIdeals, induction on the codimension). This replaces representation-finiteness as the input of the ported BGRS comparability theorem.
